relevance_note: Case report of one child with LAD-1 carrying an ITGB2 nonsense mutation and an ITGB2-spanning deletion: "We report on a child with LAD-1, dysmorphic features, and growth retardation caused by a combination of a point mutation in ITGB2 and a gross deletion resulting in r(21)."
method_note: Read the full Markdown by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script from hand-written values. The file also contains the tail of a preceding letter (lines with refs 7-9) and the start of a following, unrelated letter (placental IgG transfer); both were ignored. Three in-scope people: the patient (single unnamed case report patient, label 'patient'; the paper also calls him 'the proband'), his mother (heterozygous carrier of c.79A>T) and his father (tested negative for c.79A>T and normal on chromosomal/FISH analysis; no variant row). Values decode Markdown escapes and HTML entities (e.g. value 'c.79A > T', span 'c.79A > T'; value 'NM_000211.3', span 'NM\_000211.3'). Zygosity of c.79A>T in the patient is recorded as stated ('homozygous nonsense mutation'; Fig 1 legend 'TT'), but the paper itself shows the other ITGB2 allele is deleted (heterozygous de novo deletion spanning ITGB2 on the paternally derived allele), so the patient is functionally hemizygous for c.79A>T; the paper never uses that word. The deletion is recorded as a second ITGB2 variant row (large deletion/CNV, heterozygous, de novo: trio SNP array plus normal parental chromosome/FISH analysis); the paper says it is on the 'paternally derived allele' and also 'de novo'. Genome build for the breakpoint coordinates is not printed; the two softwares give different breakpoints, both recorded. Possible inconsistency: HSCT at 7 months and status 'At 2 years after HSCT' imply age about 31 months, yet the later sentence says 'at 18 months of age ... he remains beneath the third percentile'; age at last evaluation recorded as '18 months of age' as written. Publication year from 'Available online October 9, 2009' (the line preceding this letter; the following line 'October 28, 2009' belongs to the next letter as laid out; both are 2009). Umbilical and surgical-wound swabs grew E faecalis and C parapsilosis; the paper does not call these infections, so omphalitis, skin/soft tissue infection and fungal infection checklist items are left not reported. Growth retardation is not equated with failure to thrive (checklist not reported). 'No evidence of immune deficiency' at 18 months is after HSCT and recorded as excluded with that context. Normal lymphocyte subsets, mitogen response, IgG and IgM recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27). Herniotomy implies a hernia that is not stated, so no hernia feature row. Mother and father have no phenotype rows; all their checklist items are not reported.
